title: manihot carthagenensis
intro: Manihot carthagenensis, commonly known as the wild cassava or bussu, is a plant species native to the Americas, belonging to the Euphorbiaceae family. The leaves and roots of the wild cassava plant have been traditionally used to treat various health conditions, including fever, inflammation, and gastrointestinal issues, due to its health benefits such as anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. The therapeutic actions of Manihot carthagenensis include its ability to exhibit anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial activities, as well as its potential to modulate the immune system. The bioactive constituents of the plant include saponins, flavonoids, and alkaloids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
